mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,800K units signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero during such episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 4% for two consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% year-over-year, combined with a federal funds rate above 4%, signals a risk of deflationary pressures, which can depress corporate pricing power and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and cost of goods sold, but may also boost consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during such episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a broad-based demand recovery, which boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent federal funds rate below 2% for more than one year signals an extended period of monetary accommodation, which lowers borrowing costs and supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during periods when FEDFUNDS < 2% for more than one year (t-test p > 0.05).
